To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
long-term exposure to air pollutants, especially O(3), was associated with the occurrence of rhinosinusitis and lung function impairment, in a group of mail carriers.

(1) Mail carriers have increased risk of developing rhinitis compared to office employees; (2) The most exposed mail carriers have increased risk to develop rhinitis compared with less exposed; (3) Mail carriers have impaired lung function compared to office employees and; (4) The most exposed postal workers have impaired lung function.

1) mail carriers have a high prevalence of rhinitis symptoms; 2) mail carriers are exposed to higher levels of air pollutants compared to office employees; 3) exposure to air pollutants, particularly O(3), is significantly associated with rhinitis in mail carriers; 4) exposure to NO(2), O(3), PM(10) and CO is significantly associated with lung function impairment in the postal group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of long-term exposure to air pollution on health of a specific occupational group.
a group of workers who are exposed to air pollutants in the workplace and during their commute to work.
the effects of air pollutants on respiratory outcomes in postal employees.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
air pollution is an important factor contributing to the occurrence of respiratory symptoms and lung impairment in mail carriers, but not to a significant degree.

mail carriers are a vulnerable group to air pollution, especially to O(3), and that they may be used as a surrogate group in the study of the health effects of air pollution in the general population.
mail carriers are exposed to air pollutants at a higher rate than the general population and they have higher risk for respiratory symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mail carriers have a higher prevalence of respiratory symptoms, which is related to their occupational exposure to air pollution.
the adverse effects of air pollution are more apparent in the occupational group with higher exposure, i.e. mail carriers.
air pollution exposure is a risk factor for the occurrence and persistence of rhinitis in mail carriers and that it is a factor contributing to the development of lung function impairment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adverse effects of air pollution in postal workers are more apparent when exposure assessment is based on personal measurements.
postal workers are exposed to higher levels of pollutants and are more vulnerable to their adverse respiratory effects than office employees.
the postal workers are at risk of developing rhinitis and impaired lung function.
